passage:
The physics exam was at nine, and at half past midnight Madhav was still scrolling under the blanket, eyes burning, thumb moving on its own. He had said "one more video" about forty times. By morning his head ached, and he snapped at his little sister for asking him to pass the salt.
At school Shankar looked at him. "You look like you haven't slept, and you bit my head off yesterday too." Madhav admitted he couldn't stop at night.
They made a plan: the phone charges in the hall, an old clock for the alarm, a paperback by the bed. If it still didn't work, they would tell Madhav's father or the school counsellor together.
That night the hall charger blinked in the dark, and Madhav opened the book.

qa.q: Where does the phone charge under the plan Madhav and Shankar made?
What might Madhav be feeling when his thumb keeps moving on its own?
qa.a: He seems unable to stop, tired and frustrated, since his eyes burn and he snaps at people the next day.

qa.q: What else could Madhav do if the plan doesn't work?
qa.a: He could tell his father or the school counsellor, as Shankar suggests, because asking for help is wise if he feels unable to change.

qa.q: How might Madhav's little sister have felt when he snapped about the salt?
qa.a: She may have felt confused or hurt, since she only asked for salt; the snap likely came from his tiredness, not from her.

grounding: Shows a teen unable to stop late-night scrolling, tired and irritable, making a phone-outside plan and a fallback of telling adults.

passage:
Tuesday night, 11:40

I'm writing this instead of scrolling. That's the experiment.

Last night I was on my phone till 2:15. Again. I only meant to watch "one more" video. Then it was five more. This morning I couldn't get up, missed breakfast and snapped at Disha when she asked for the salt. She's nine. She looked so hurt. I felt horrible about it all day.

In maths I kept putting my head down. Sir asked if I was sick.

I think I actually can't stop on my own. So I tried something. I plugged the phone in the kitchen at ten and borrowed Disha's comic book. The first twenty minutes were awful. My hand kept reaching for my pocket.

Then it got easier. It's 11:40 and I'm sleepy. Real sleepy.

If this doesn't work by the weekend, I'll tell Mummy and ask her to keep the phone at night. I said sorry to Disha before bed. She gave me the comic.

Vishal

qa.q: What time was Vishal on the phone till last night?
qa.a: Vishal was on the phone till 2:15.

qa.q: What did Vishal feel after snapping at Disha?
qa.a: Vishal felt horrible and guilty all day, because Disha is nine and looked so hurt.

qa.q: What plan is Vishal trying, and what is the backup?
qa.a: Vishal is charging the phone in the kitchen and reading a comic instead, and if it doesn't work by the weekend, Vishal will ask Mummy to keep the phone at night.

qa.q: How might Disha feel when Vishal apologises?
qa.a: Disha seems to feel better and forgiving, since she gave Vishal her comic.

grounding: It shows a teen who cannot stop scrolling late at night and is tired and irritable, charging the phone outside the room, planning an alternative and ready to talk to a parent.
